description: Default architecture with random init; logs the task interface and forward inputs (baseline, expected ~0% accuracy).

One block, no LayerNorm: lookup-table attention reads x_j=sum (a_k+b_k)10^(j-k) with '+' as sink; 20-ReLU MLP maps x to a mod-10 polygon ring; head picks the sector. NOT EXACT: 200/200 on eval but 124 of 50658 wrong in the stress test (border offset too large).
RingAttnV1 with the border offset fixed to half the true finest step (1e-5 at the final-carry step); V1 passed 200/200 but failed near-99999 sums in the stress test.

RingAttnV2 without model.double(): tests whether default float32 has enough precision for the 5e-6 border margin. NOT EXACT: 200/200 on eval but 1 of 50658 wrong in the stress test (89999+90001). First attempt crashed on a dtype mismatch before logging; fixed and rerun under this name.
d_model 17 to 11: output steps reuse the key dims as query one-hots; the off-key dim keeps answer tokens from ever being attended to.
Residual connections removed so attention and MLP outputs can reuse dims, taking d_model from 11 to 8.
ReLU polygon replaced by a cos/sin activation with one hidden angle (d_ff=1): x turns the mod-10 ring exactly, as in the grokking Fourier circuits.
RingCosineD8 minus W_k and W_o: keys are the raw embeddings and W_v applies the single 1/ALPHA gain, so W_q alone holds the attention table.
fc2 removed; the 12x2 head reads (cos, sin) directly, so each digit's head row is literally its sector centre on the unit circle.
Keys come only from pos_emb (7-dim) and values only from a scalar token_emb; W_q holds the attention table, so W_v and the wide embeddings are gone.
fc1 removed: token embeddings are angles, attention takes their place-weighted mean, a parameter-free (cos, sin) reads it, and the head is rotated by the border offset.
Attention reads only the 11 tokens aaaaa+bbbbb, so answer tokens need no off-key and d_model drops from 7 to 6.
Higher columns add whole turns of the mod-10 ring, so they need no masking: plain dot-product softmax attention with rank-2 place values plus a sink, d_model=3, no W_q.
d_model=2: the '+' key is the origin (score 0), so one solved per-step query scale t sets the softmax gain and shifts the decimal point with no separate sink dim.
Head tied to the token embeddings: logit_t = cos(z - gain e_t - phase), so a digit's input and output angle are one number; '+' and '=' are masked from the output.
No ring or periodic unit: causal attention subtracts the digits already written to get a remainder in [0,10), and a plain linear head with quadratic templates reads floor(R).
Original 64-dim, 4-head, 3-layer, ReLU, LayerNorm, residual architecture unmodified: balanced zero-mean constant-norm embeddings make LayerNorm a constant, and ReLU kinks sit at the warped y(n).
Float32 schoolbook circuit: one head reads a_j and b_j, a second reads the tail, a two-ReLU step turns tail >= 1 into a carry bit, and an integer ring gives (a+b+c) mod 10.
Schoolbook circuit in float32 with only attention, ReLU and linear layers: carry bit from the tail, two more ReLUs subtract 10 when z >= 10, and a linear template head reads the digit.
Two-layer carry lookahead: layer 1 codes each column kill/propagate/generate, layer 2 reads the codes as a base-3 fraction where carry means T > 1/2, widening the threshold gap enough for float16.
Content-based carry scan in float16: layer 1 flags each column decisive/generate, and layer 2 attention lands on the nearest decisive column below and copies its generate bit, with no threshold.
CarryScanAttnFloat16 rechecked on all 7^5 column-sum patterns over {0,7,8,9,10,11,18}, each randomly split into digits, which exercises every propagate chain.
Carry scan with smaller integer constants (NEAR 3, DECIDE 24, OFF -32, PAIR 12), softening attention to see how far the circuit stays exact.
Carry scan pushed to NEAR 2, DECIDE 14, OFF -20, PAIR 8 to find where softened attention stops being exact; expected to fail through the mod-10 detector.
Same tiny constants as CarryScanTinyInts, with the mod-10 detector sharpened into a step flat within 0.25 of every integer so that a soft carry cannot leak through the times-10 fold.
Sharp-wrap carry scan with NEAR 1, DECIDE 8, OFF -12, PAIR 6, the softest attention tried, to bracket the limit at which the scan itself stops being exact.
RingTiedHead with one embedding per place value: a_c and b_c share a slot, so the position table shrinks to 12 rows (5 columns, the '+' origin, 6 output steps).
Negative control: RingSharedSlots without model.double(), measuring how badly the whole-sum ring (x up to 2e5, borders 1e-5 wide) degrades in default float32.
Back in float64, with token embeddings replaced by digit * one scalar and the head by a scalar turn and phase, leaving the 12-row position table as the only table.
RingLinearTokens verified on 1,000,000 random pairs plus the edge, complement and column-pattern sets, also reporting the smallest top-1 vs top-2 logit margin.
